NON MEDICAL STAFF GIVING FALSE KNOWLEDGE! If I could give less than 1 star I would.

As a pregnant patient, I was provided with incorrect medical information by non-clinical staff (the receptionist) regarding vaccinations.

The information given was later contradicted by qualified doctors at Harrogate hospital who were outraged at this practices false information to me. This is not a minor administrative issue, it is a clinical one. Providing inaccurate medical advice to a pregnant woman has potential huge implications and should never occur. The fact that a receptionist thinks they can give medical knowledge, wrong medical knowledge at that is worrying. And I worry who else they do this to?

What is particularly concerning is that medical queries were not escalated to a clinician when raised. Non-clinical staff should not be advising on clinical matters without confirmation from a qualified professional. When challenged by myself to said receptionist from what I was previous told by my midwife she doubled down saying she was correct and that it was fine. She pushed for me to book something I shouldn’t have, this is not okay.

There was also no acknowledgment or apology once the misinformation became apparent to me. I was told that it “would be escalated” but it was clear that it was not from the fact I did not receive even a text or call acknowledging their huge mistake or tell me the steps they have taken to make sure this doesn’t happen again. On a patient care level this is not okay. Patient care should be a priority - clearly not here.

The practice should urgently review its procedures to ensure that pregnant patients or any patient are given accurate, clinician-verified guidance not given false information from receptionists with 0 medical training who just answer phones. If a patient asks a medical question or query of a medical nature they should know to not answer and to follow up with the GP. Making up information is dangerous.

It’s disappointing to see how this situation was handled and I will be processing it further to a NHS complaint as advised because of the severity of this incident.

I am new to this practice, and have always heard mixed reviews but sadly this shows that the ones who have been mistreated or had wrong information told to them are true.

I called the other day and spoke to a young girl on the phone trying to book an appointment for my Grandma, she was unwell with a number of things. The young girl I spoke to was very well mannered, kind and understanding. The information was “passed to the duty team” a process I found confusing as I felt she needed to be seen in person. I queried this and the young girl explained they use a ‘triage’ system, so we’d get a text with an appointment and that the reception team no longer book emergency appointments. It makes total sense to do it this way as I’d sooner a doctor decide how quickly my grandmother is to be seen than a receptionist. We got a message, as promised, within 10 minutes inviting us for an appointment within 2 hours. The doctor we saw (I couldn’t catch the name but I think it may have been Dr. Ganeeshi) was brilliant, caring kind and dealt with my frail Grandma very well. We then had to book some bloods and collect some sample pots, so we popped back to reception and spoke to a young man called Ben. It was refreshing to see a young man working reception and he himself dealt with my grandmother with a sense of patience (she often gets confused) and care, his colleague who I believe was called Beth was on the other side of the desk and I think it may have been her I spoke to on the phone earlier in the day. Both receptionists had a great deal of empathy both with my grandmother and each patient (there were many) I saw them deal with. It’s incredibly refreshing to see such lovely receptionists, being able to have both tricky and positive interactions, it’s rare you hear of GP receptionists smiling! But it’s clear they both care a great deal about what they do. Based on all of this, I may become a Spa Surgery patient myself! Thank you all for your care and kindness, even with the NHS the way it is you all continue to be so supportive. My only gripe? Please inform your patients if you change systems.
